newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures down in light, cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures down in light, cautious trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were lower in light, early trade, as the tone remained short-term bearish from Tuesday's sell-off, traders said.
"All the important data for the month is already out," one T-bond futures trader said, referring to U.S. May consumer and producer prices.
"And I think the failure to test the upside yesterday will keep the bid light today," he said.
September T-bonds fell to Tuesday's low of 111-17/32, below trendline support at 111-18/32. One firm bought 500 contracts, pushing September to 111-20/32.
Preliminary open interest on Tuesday declined with prices, but traders attributed the decrease to June T-bonds' expiration on Thursday, June 19.
They also said the expiration of July T-bond and T-note options on futures on Friday could sway price action in the futures pits.

In the meantime, revised data on U.S. factory orders and first-quarter productivity will be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, and could generate activity. Productivity is expected to rise 2.1 percent, compared to up 2.0 percent, and unit labor costs are forecast to gain 2.6 percent, from up 2.7 percent.
However, traders said the May consumer and producer price data has already convinced the market that U.S. inflationary pressures remain tame.
"Even before the numbers, crude oil and the energy complex as a whole are telling you that we're in a low inflationary environment," one T-bond futures trader said.
Resistance is at Tuesday's high of 112-10/32, 112-14/32, and at 112-27/32. Support is at 110-23/32, a 38.2-percent retracement level from the contract's rally to 112-10/32 from 108-05/32.
At 0828 CDT/1328 GMT, September T-bonds were off 08/32 at 111-20/32 and December Eurodollars were off 0.025 at 93.925. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
